thread:
sam: starting canary for release/2.13.0 to canary-cluster-42. rolling 5% of traffic now. will watch health checks and latency.
ops-bot: ALERT: canary-cluster-42 - http_5xx_rate increased to 4.8% (5m avg) threshold 1.0%. triggered at 03:03:17 UTC.
maria: saw same on dashboard, traces show a burst of backend 502s around 03:03. not every pod, looks concentrated on node-gpu-3.
sam: confirmed. tailing logs now.
leo: @sam can you paste the failed request pattern? might be an upstream timeout.
sam: logs snippet: ```
[03:03:12] upstream request to storage-proxy timed out after 1.2s, status=502
[03:03:12] retrying request id=abcd1234
[03:03:12] socket error: ECONNRESET
```
pri ya: (typo) priya: looking at probe latencies: liveness probes latency 95p jumped from 60ms to 550ms across canary pods. readiness still passing for most but flapping on 2/8.
leo: interesting — probe latency spike could be GC pause or network. any correlation with deploy hooks?
sam: deploy-bot logged rollout step: `applied config -> 5%` at 03:01:48. no config changes to probes.
ops-bot: METRICS: request_latency_p95_canary=560ms, baseline_p95=48ms. error_rate_5m=4.8%.
maria: customer impact? any errors hitting production routes?
sam: 5xxs are showing on the canary route only so far, but traffic is mirrored from prod paths. customers not widely affected yet. still possible if we continue rollout.
leo: recommend immediate abort - we have abort criteria: 5m 5xx > 2% OR p95 > 300ms. both hit.
priya: oncall, I'm prepping rollback steps and a feature-flag toggle. which we want?
sam: feature-flag exists for new handler (ff/new-routing). turning it off will route to stable.
leo: turning off ff is faster. rollback will take longer because of multi-region cache warming.
sre-lead: prioritize minimal blast radius. flip feature flag first, abort the canary rollout. call it in incident timeline.
maria: agree. @sam can you flip the flag and monitor for 2 minutes? I'll watch metrics and K/V cache errors.
sam: flipping ff/new-routing -> off now. 
ops-bot: ACTION: feature flag ff/new-routing set to OFF by sam at 03:05:22 UTC. traffic routed to stable variant.
sam: running quick smoke: `curl -sS https://canary.example.internal/health | jq .` returns `{"status":"ok"}` on most pods, but still 1 pod showing high probe delay.
leo: good. watching the 5xx curve...
ops-bot: METRICS: request_latency_p95_canary dropped to 78ms in 90s, error_rate_5m down to 0.9%.
priya: looks like flip helped. can we abort rollout in deployment controller to be safe?
sam: aborting rollout now: `kubectl rollout undo deployment/api-service --namespace=canary` -> started.
deploy-bot: Rollout abort initiated by sam (rollback to revision 23). progress events: 2/8 updated -> 0/8 updated.
leo: good. tag this as "canary-abort-ff-fallback" in timeline.
sre-lead: capturing timeline and customer-impact: no external 5xx spike observed on prod; canary saw transient 4.8% 5xx for ~3m before mitigation; no incidents escalated to customers.
maria: confirmed. create incident ticket? I can open P0 if we had customer-facing impact; this is P2 candidate.
sam: opening ticket: INC-2007 in ops board with tags: canary, deploy-failure, probe-latency.
priya: next steps: analyze cause (GC vs network), collect heap/metrics from node-gpu-3 and pod logs for the 03:00-03:10 window. assign to infra/observability.
leo: also add a runbook update to checklist: require probe latency validation step before canary >5%.
sre-lead: agreed. I'll own the follow-up and assign postmortem to infra the next sprint. thanks all for quick flip. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: NOTE: on-call handoff: sam -> leo in 35m.
sam: handing off to @leo for monitoring and post-rollback verification. I'll be reachable but moving to other tasks.
leo: taking over. will keep watch for 20 more mins then mark thread resolved if stable. :eyes:
